**[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
***A [[Russian Armed Forces|Russia]]n [[missile]] strikes a major [[thermal power station]] in [[Burshtyn]], [[Ivano-Frankivsk Oblast]], [[Ukraine]], causing "quite serious damage", according to [[governor]] [[Svitlana Onyshchuk]]. **A 17-year-old protester, Abolfazl Adinezadeh, is killed in the city of [[Mashhad]] by [[Basij|Iranian security forces]], who shot him at [[point-blank range]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/world-middle-east-63328086 (BBC News)]
*[[2022 Belarusian and Russian partisan movement]]
**[[Opposition to Vladimir Putin in Russia|Anti-Kremlin]] [[Bashkirs|Bashkir]] [[Free Idel-Ural|nationalists]] announce the creation of "The Committee of Bashkir Resistance", with the aim of [[Dissolution of Russia|achieving independence]] for [[Bashkortostan]], although the committee had already been established in September. '''Disasters and accidents'''
*Telecommunication between the [[Shetland]] islands and the [[Great Britain|British mainland]] is interrupted when a [[subsea cable]] is damaged. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-scotland-north-east-orkney-shetland-63326102 (BBC News)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in China]]
***Additional restrictions are imposed in [[Beijing]] as the number of positive [[COVID-19]] cases quadruples in the city. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2022/oct/20/beijing-steps-up-covid-measures-as-cases-quadruple-during-key-ccp-congress-meeting (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*The [[Australian Capital Territory]] decriminalizes the possession of illicit drugs in small quantities, including [[cocaine]], [[amphetamine]]s and [[heroin]] beginning in October 2023. Those caught with illicit drugs for [[recreational drug use|personal use]] will be fined or referred to [[drug rehabilitation]] programs. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2022/oct/20/act-becomes-first-australian-jurisdiction-to-decriminalise-illicit-drugs-in-small-quantities (''The Guardian'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Death of Harry Dunn]]
**Anne Sacoolas, the wife of a US diplomat, pleads guilty at the [[Old Bailey]] (via video link from the USA), to causing the death of British teenage motorcyclist Harry Dunn by [[careless driving]]. [https://abcnews.go.com/International/anne-sacoolas-wife-us-diplomat-pleads-guilty-death/story?id=91791741 (ABC News)], [https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2022/oct/20/anne-sacoolas-admits-causing-death-of-harry-dunn (''The Guardian'')]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Premiership of Liz Truss]]
**[[October 2022 United Kingdom government crisis]]
***An investigation is launched into a [[House of Commons of the United Kingdom|Commons]] vote on [[Hydraulic fracturing|fracking]] where several [[Conservative Party (UK)|Tory]] [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|MPs]] were allegedly bullied, manhandled, and verbally abused. The 40 [[Conservative Party (UK)|ruling party]] MPs who [[Party discipline|failed to back the government]] in the vote now face disciplinary action in the form of losing the [[Whip (politics)#United Kingdom|whip]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/oct/19/crunch-commons-vote-on-fracking-descends-into-farce (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-63322533 (BBC News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/fracking-tory-mps-trevelyan-vote-b2206624.html (''The Independent'')] [https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2022/oct/20/dozens-tory-mps-facing-disciplinary-action-fracking-vote (''The Guardian'' 2)]
***[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|Prime Minister]] [[Liz Truss]] announces her [[resignation]], to take effect once a [[October 2022 Conservative Party leadership election|replacement has been appointed]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/live/uk-politics-63309400 (BBC News)]
